card.name: Table cell boundaries in dosing tables
card.fires_on: A word or symbol at the join between table cells or rows in flattened label tables, such as arrows, a row heading, or the start of a new row label. It fires where one entry ends and the next begins.

modes.label: Arrows in interaction tables
modes.description: Up or down arrows giving a change in AUC or Cmax after a drug and dose.
modes.example: ↔ ↔ Clarithromycin 500 mg twice a day 300 mg once a day HIV-infected patients (12)<< ↑>> AUC by 75% ↓

modes.label: Row or column heading words
modes.description: A word starting or ending a table label, such as a method heading or a condition name.
modes.example: FERTILITY PER 100,000 NONSTERILE WOMEN, BY FERTILITY CONTROL METHOD ACCORDING TO AGE Method<< of>> control and outcome 15-1

card.plain: It marks the spot where one table cell runs into the next in a flattened dosing or interaction table.
